subject: POC workload handshake: concurrency, burst patterns & success roadmap
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finline.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC workload handshake: concurrency, burst patterns & success roadmap

Hi Olivia — great conversation today, appreciate the clear description of Finline's ingestion pattern. Per our call, I wanted to capture the initial handshake and next steps so we can scope the POC traffic model and agree success criteria. I've attached a quick CSV template for the workload snapshot and our POC playbook.

Summary of what you shared (please correct any mistakes):
- Primary use case: document summarization + metadata extraction for transaction logs (approx ~120 tokens per summary).
- Production target: 2000 daily users; early POC test will route a subset of traffic (ingest/front-end) to Redwood for 2 weeks.
- Observed peak: 220 requests/minute during settlement window (8–9am PST), short spikes up to ~450 RPS for ~40s during batch close.
- Average request token length: prompt ~80 tokens, expected model response ~150 tokens (total average around 230 tokens).
- Typical concurrency from app: 30–60 concurrent requests; burst windows push concurrency to ~250 for under a minute.

Proposed POC traffic profile (for alignment):
- Baseline: 50 RPS sustained for business-hours simulation (8am–6pm PST).
- Peak window: 450 RPS simulated for repeated 40s bursts every 10 minutes during a 1-hour test window.
- Concurrency targets: 60 steady, with engineered bursts up to 300 concurrent to test autoscaling and cold-start behavior.

Success criteria (draft):
1) Latency: p95 generation latency <= 850ms for baseline; p95 <= 1.8s during burst windows with fallback behavior documented.
2) Cost: per-token cost within 15% of our projected budget target for the POC (we'll provide your cost baseline).
3) Stability: zero 5xx errors attributable to capacity for traffic within the tested profiles; graceful throttling/fallback for overflow.
4) Output quality: automated eval pass rate >= 88% on the seed prompt set we discussed.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Olivia: share a 48-hr sample of request logs or complete the attached workload snapshot CSV (finline-workload-snapshot.csv) by EOD Thu 8/27.
- Logan: stand up the POC environment and send a test ingestion harness + runner (target: staging link) by Fri 8/28.
- Monica: define monitoring dashboards and SLOs; draft cost projection and batching/quantization recommendations.
- Karthik: validate model variant choices and quantization compatibility for the token lengths above.

Attachments: finline-workload-snapshot.csv (template), redwood-poc-eval-playbook.pdf (POC steps + eval harness).

Thanks — if this looks right, reply with timestamps for the 48-hr sample and any corrections to the traffic figures.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finline.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC workload handshake: concurrency, burst patterns & success roadmap

Thanks Logan — this is very helpful and matches our notes. A couple of clarifications: 
- The 450 "RPS" I quoted was shorthand for "requests per minute" during the window; sorry for the confusion. The actual spike we see is ~7.5 RPS sustained for ~40s (which corresponds to the batch close fan-out).
- Concurrency: our front-end maintains a connection pool per service instance; in practice we expect 30 steady concurrency with a realistic worst-case of ~120 during a multi-tenant roll-up.
- Token lengths: some documents (invoices) can go longer — up to 800 tokens in the prompt; however this is rare (~2% of traffic).

I'll attach the requested sample logs to a secure S3 link and fill the CSV by EOD Thursday. Quick question on the success criteria: for output quality, can we include one manual review step (10 blind checks) in addition to automated evals?

On the manual review I'm happy to own coordinating the reviewers — we want to make sure edge-case invoices aren't regressed.

Olivia
Olivia Chen
Director, Data Products — Finline Systems
olivia.chen@finline.com | +1 415-666-2020

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finline.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC workload handshake: concurrency, burst patterns & success roadmap

Perfect — thanks for the clarifications, Olivia. Quick notes after your reply: 
- We'll assume RPS numbers in true "requests per second" for our load generator; thanks for confirming the minute/second mix. We'll model both the steady-state and the 7.5 RPS batch spikes you described, plus a safety burst factor to exercise autoscaling.
- For the rare long prompts (~800 tokens), we'll run a specific long-tail test (5% of test load) to validate the KV-cache behavior and memory footprint.
- Manual review: yes — we support combining automated evals with a 10-sample manual blind check. We'll include that as a gated quality step in the POC signoff.

Action items updated: 
- Olivia: S3 sample logs + filled CSV by Thu 2026-08-27 EOD (owner: Finline).
- Logan: POC staging link + synthetic workload generator (two profiles: steady + batch spikes) by Fri 2026-08-28 EOD.
- Monica: monitoring dashboard (p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, token usage, concurrency, cost-rate) and a cost projection doc by Tue 2026-08-31.
- Karthik: recommend model variant and quantization profile; include expected token-cost delta for the 800-token path by Tue 2026-08-31.

I'll send a short calendar invite proposing 3x30m sessions next week: 1) POC kickoff (env + access), 2) mid-point traffic run, 3) quality review & signoff.

— Logan

Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC workload handshake: concurrency, burst patterns & success roadmap

Thanks — received the S3 link and the filled CSV (Olivia, great turnaround). Quick internal notes and a proposed runbook for our staging load: 

1) Workload generator profiles (already checked into staging repo):
- profile-steady.json -> 50 RPS sustained, concurrency target 60, duration 1 hour
- profile-batch.json -> repeated 40s bursts at 7.5 RPS with 10s cool-down, repeated for 30 minutes
- profile-longtail.json -> 5% of requests at ~800 prompt tokens, interspersed randomly

2) Monitoring & SLOs (dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/POC-8391)
- p50/p95/p99 latency for generation calls (model-side), token consumption per minute, 5xx rate, instance CPU/mem, queue length
- Alert: 5xx > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes -> page oncall infra and notify Olivia

3) Cost/runbook notes:
- We'll enable intelligent batching for baseline to reduce per-token cost; for batch-spike windows we'll disable aggressive batching to preserve latency targets.
- Expected incremental cost uplift for long prompts ~20–30% per request — Karthik please confirm exact delta in your recommendation doc.

4) Timeline checkpoints:
- Fri 8/28: staging link + generator (Logan) — complete
- Mon 8/31: first controlled run and monitoring baseline (all)
- Wed 9/02: mid-point quality review (manual 10-sample + automated eval)
- Fri 9/04: POC readout and signoff recommendation (stakeholders: Logan, Monica, Karthik, Olivia)

I'll draft a shared checklist in the Drive folder and tag the dashboards in the invite. Karthik — can you post the model variant recommendations by EOD Tue 8/31? I'll include cost modeling in the Drive doc.

— Monica Patel
Solutions Ops, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0147
